1	# Stability and analysis options in Pynite
2	
3	This is a lightly formatted copy of the official Pynite manual at the
4	pre-fix source revision.  It is included as public scientific evidence, not as
5	an implementation hint.  Source: <https://github.com/JWock82/Pynite/blob/147c7aa24ec30b1c6a4d4820446915380752877b/docs/source/stability.rst>
6	and <https://github.com/JWock82/Pynite/blob/147c7aa24ec30b1c6a4d4820446915380752877b/docs/source/analysis.rst>.
7	
8	In a three-dimensional model, an object can translate in X, Y, or Z and rotate
9	about X, Y, or Z.  These three translations and three rotations are six
10	degrees of freedom, and all six must be stabilized for an object to be stable.
11	Rigid-body motion occurs when the entire structure can move as a unit because
12	supports are insufficient.  Localized nodal instabilities can remain after the
13	global structure is supported; hinged-ended members meeting at a node are one
14	example described by the manual.  Both situations appear as a singular,
15	unsolvable stiffness system.
16	
17	Pynite exposes a `check_stability=True` option on analysis methods to help
18	isolate these cases.  The manual also notes that the option costs extra
19	analysis time and is normally enabled while debugging a model.
20	
21	The analysis guide documents sparse and dense matrix solvers.  Sparse storage
22	keeps non-zero entries and is the default when SciPy is available; dense mode
23	stores all entries and can be useful for small models.  General analysis is
24	available through `FEModel3D.analyze()`, while `analyze_linear()` assembles a
25	linear model once and superposes load combinations.  These paths are both
26	used by the public workbench.
27	
28	Pynite's manual further distinguishes second-order P-Delta effects from the
29	first-order stability questions exercised here.  The workbench uses static
30	first-order cases so that the observations can be repeated without plotting,
31	network access, or external data.
32

34	see `source/LICENSE`.

# stiffness matrices. A free stiffness submatrix that is singular to working
# precision (e.g. rigid-body motion or an internal mechanism) produces at least

def _solve_stiffness(K11, RHS, sparse: bool = True):
    """Solves the partitioned stiffness system ``K11 D1 = RHS`` for the unknown nodal displacements.

    Detection of singular stiffness systems is part of solving: directly solving a
    singular matrix can silently return nondeterministic garbage (and the sparse

# Relative factorization-pivot tolerance used to detect a singular stiffness system. A
# stiffness submatrix for the unrestrained degrees of freedom that is singular to working
# precision (rigid-body motion or an internal mechanism) produces at least one factorization
# pivot of essentially zero magnitude compared to the matrix's own stiffness scale, while a
# properly restrained structure stays many orders of magnitude above this threshold. Direct
# solvers do not reliably report such systems: the dense solver only fails on an exactly
# zero pivot, and the sparse solver can return unbounded, solver-dependent garbage without
# raising or even warning. Singularity therefore has to be checked as part of the solution.
_PIVOT_TOLERANCE = 1e-13


def _solve_stiffness(K11: NDArray[float64] | 'lil_matrix', RHS: NDArray[float64], sparse: bool = True) -> NDArray[float64]:
    """Solves the partitioned stiffness system `K11 D1 = RHS` for the unknown nodal displacements.

    A stiffness matrix that is singular to working precision indicates an unstable structure
    (rigid-body motion or a mechanism). Rather than returning meaningless displacements, an
    exception is raised when the factorization reveals such a singular matrix.

    :param K11: The partitioned stiffness submatrix for the unrestrained degrees of freedom.
    :param RHS: The right-hand-side vector for the unrestrained degrees of freedom.
    :param sparse: Indicates whether `K11` is stored sparsely (`True`) or densely (`False`). Defaults to True.
    :type sparse: bool, optional
    :raises Exception: Occurs when the stiffness matrix is singular (rigid body motion or a mechanism). This indicates an unstable structure has been modeled.
    :return: The displacements of the unrestrained degrees of freedom.
    """

    # Factor the stiffness matrix with the requested solver
    if sparse == True:
        from scipy.sparse.linalg import splu

        try:
            # Factor the sparse stiffness matrix. `splu` raises an error only when the
            # matrix is exactly singular.
            lu = splu(K11.tocsc())
        except Exception:
            # Return out of the method if 'K11' is singular and provide an error message
            raise Exception('The stiffness matrix is singular, which implies rigid body motion. The structure is unstable. Aborting analysis.')

        # Extract the factorization pivots and the equation solver
        pivots = lu.U.diagonal()
        factor_solve = lu.solve

    else:
        from scipy.linalg import lu_factor, lu_solve

        # Factor the dense stiffness matrix. `lu_factor` only warns (rather than raising an
        # error) when the matrix is exactly singular, so the pivots must be checked below.
        lu_piv = lu_factor(K11)

        # Extract the factorization pivots and the equation solver
        pivots = lu_piv[0].diagonal()
        def factor_solve(b):
            return lu_solve(lu_piv, b)

    # Check for a numerically singular stiffness matrix. A singular system appears as a
    # pivot of essentially zero magnitude relative to the stiffness scale of the matrix, and
    # solving such a system cannot produce a meaningful displacement vector.
    scale = abs(K11.diagonal()).max() if K11.shape[0] > 0 else 0.0
    if abs(pivots).min() <= scale * _PIVOT_TOLERANCE:
        # Return out of the method if 'K11' is singular and provide an error message
        raise Exception('The stiffness matrix is singular, which implies rigid body motion. The structure is unstable. Aborting analysis.')

    # Calculate the unknown displacements
    return factor_solve(RHS)

"""Regression tests for the static-analysis stability repair.

These tests exercise the documented contract of the public analysis paths
(`analyze` / `analyze_linear`, sparse and dense solvers):

* Supported structures produce finite, solver-consistent results.
* Structures whose stiffness systems are singular to working precision
  (rigid-body motion or a mechanism) raise instead of silently returning
  unbounded, solver-dependent garbage.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

TASK_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(TASK_ROOT / 'source'))

from Pynite import FEModel3D  # noqa: E402

E = 29000.0
G = 11200.0
NU = 0.3
RHO = 0.284
A = 10.0
IY = 100.0
IZ = 150.0
J = 250.0


def _beam_model(nodes, members, supports, load, release=None):
    model = FEModel3D()
    model.add_material('steel', E, G, NU, RHO)
    model.add_section('S', A, IY, IZ, J)
    for name, x, y, z in nodes:
        model.add_node(name, x, y, z)
    for name, i, j in members:
        model.add_member(name, i, j, 'steel', 'S')
    for node, flags in supports.items():
        model.def_support(node, *flags)
    model.add_node_load(*load)
    if release is not None:
        member, dof = release
        model.def_releases(member, **{dof: True})
    return model


def _cantilever():
    # 144-inch cantilever column with a 10-kip transverse tip load
    return _beam_model(
        nodes=[('n1', 0, 0, 0), ('n2', 0, 144, 0)],
        members=[('m1', 'n1', 'n2')],
        supports={'n1': (True, True, True, True, True, True)},
        load=('n2', 'FY', 10.0),
    )


def _portal_frame():
    # The supported control frame: bases fixed, lateral sway load
    return _beam_model(
        nodes=[('b1', 0, 0, 0), ('t1', 0, 144, 0), ('t2', 180, 144, 0), ('b2', 180, 0, 0)],
        members=[('c1', 'b1', 't1'), ('c2', 'b2', 't2'), ('beam', 't1', 't2')],
        supports={'b1': (True, True, True, True, True, True),
                  'b2': (True, True, True, True, True, True)},
        load=('t1', 'FX', 10.0),
    )


def _flat_three_hinge_beam():
    # Collinear pinned-pinned continuous beam with an internal moment release:
    # a kinematic mechanism whose stiffness matrix is singular to working precision.
    return _beam_model(
        nodes=[('p1', 0, 0, 0), ('p2', 130, 0, 0), ('p3', 310, 0, 0), ('p4', 450, 0, 0)],
        members=[('m1', 'p1', 'p2'), ('m2', 'p2', 'p3'), ('m3', 'p3', 'p4')],
        supports={'p1': (True, True, True, True, True, False),
                  'p4': (True, True, True, True, True, False)},
        load=('p2', 'FY', 6.0),
        release=('m2', 'Rzi'),
    )


def _free_structure():
    # No restraints at all: rigid-body motion.
    return _beam_model(
        nodes=[('n1', 0, 0, 0), ('n2', 120, 0, 0)],
        members=[('m1', 'n1', 'n2')],
        supports={},
        load=('n2', 'FY', 5.0),
    )


def test_supported_structures_finish_finite_and_consistent():
    for build in (_cantilever, _portal_frame):
        results = {}
        for method in ('analyze', 'analyze_linear'):
            for sparse in (True, False):
                model = build()
                getattr(model, method)(sparse=sparse, check_stability=True)
                tip = model.nodes[max(model.nodes, key=str)]
                results[(method, sparse)] = tip.DY['Combo 1']
                assert abs(results[(method, sparse)]) < 1e6
        base = results[('analyze', True)]
        for value in results.values():
            assert value == pytest.approx(base, rel=1e-6)


def test_cantilever_matches_beam_theory():
    # Vertical member along +Y: local y = global -X, so local-z bending of the
    # column acts in the Y direction; delta = P L^3 / (3 E I)
    model = _cantilever()
    model.analyze(check_stability=True)
    delta = model.nodes['n2'].DY['Combo 1']
    assert delta == pytest.approx(10.0 * 144.0**3 / (3 * E * IY), rel=1e-3)


def test_mechanism_structure_raises_on_all_paths():
    for method in ('analyze', 'analyze_linear'):
        for sparse in (True, False):
            model = _flat_three_hinge_beam()
            with pytest.raises(Exception, match='singular'):
                getattr(model, method)(sparse=sparse, check_stability=True)
            # The documented option being relaxed must not restore garbage results
            model = _flat_three_hinge_beam()
            with pytest.raises(Exception):
                getattr(model, method)(sparse=sparse, check_stability=False)


def test_free_structure_raises():
    for sparse in (True, False):
        model = _free_structure()
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            model.analyze(sparse=sparse, check_stability=True)
        model = _free_structure()
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            model.analyze_linear(sparse=sparse, check_stability=True)


def test_unsupported_connected_node_still_flagged_by_nodal_check():
    # A node whose translation in Z is not restrained by supports or by any
    # member stiffness: the documented nodal-instability diagnostic still works.
    model = FEModel3D()
    model.add_material('steel', E, G, NU, RHO)
    model.add_section('S', A, IY, IZ, J)
    model.add_node('n1', 0, 0, 0)
    model.add_node('n2', 120, 0, 0)
    model.add_node('n3', 240, 0, 0)  # floating in Z, connected only in-plane
    model.add_member('m1', 'n1', 'n2', 'steel', 'S')
    # n3 not connected to anything: its DOFs are exactly zero on the diagonal
    model.def_support('n1', True, True, True, True, True, True)
    model.def_support('n2', True, True, True, True, True, True)
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        model.analyze(check_stability=True)


def test_plate_with_drilling_springs_still_solves():
    # Quads rely on deliberately weak drilling springs; a supported plate must
    # not be misclassified as singular by the new singularity detection.
    model = FEModel3D()
    model.add_material('steel', E, G, NU, RHO)
    model.add_node('n1', 0, 0, 0)
    model.add_node('n2', 12, 0, 0)
    model.add_node('n3', 12, 12, 0)
    model.add_node('n4', 0, 12, 0)
    model.add_quad('q1', 'n1', 'n2', 'n3', 'n4', 0.25, 'steel')
    model.def_support('n1', True, True, True, True, True, True)
    model.def_support('n2', True, True, True, True, True, True)
    model.def_support('n3', True, True, True, True, True, True)
    model.def_support('n4', True, True, True, True, True, True)
    for sparse in (True, False):
        m2 = model.duplicate() if hasattr(model, 'duplicate') else model
        m2.analyze(sparse=sparse, check_stability=True)


def test_pdelta_path_also_protected():
    # Stable frame still converges through the P-Delta path (exercises the helper)
    model = _portal_frame()
    model.analyze_PDelta(check_stability=True)
    assert model.nodes['t1'].DX['Combo 1'] != 0
    # Mechanism must raise, not return garbage
    model = _flat_three_hinge_beam()
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        model.analyze_PDelta(check_stability=True)

## Diagnosis

`frame_b` is a genuinely unsupported configuration per the documented semantics in `paper.md`: four collinear nodes, both ends pinned with global-Z rotation free, plus an `Rzi` moment release at `m2`'s i-end — a flat three-hinged chain. First-order kinematics show a rigid mechanism, and the partitioned stiffness matrix `K11` confirms it numerically (min eigenvalue ≈ 2.3e-11, reciprocal condition ≈ 1e-16).

The documented contract says such a singular stiffness system means an unstable structure and analysis must abort. But the snapshot silently returned garbage: `numpy.linalg.solve` only raises on an *exactly* zero pivot, and `spsolve` returned unbounded, solver-dependent values (1.07e17 vs 3.14e17, with solver-dependent reactions) without even warning. - **`Analysis.py`** — added `_solve_stiffness(K11, RHS, sparse)`: factors the partitioned system (`splu` / `lu_factor`, same engines as before), then rejects the system when the smallest factorization pivot is ≤ the matrix stiffness scale × `1e-13` (machine-precision-anchored). Legit models sit ≥ ~1e-3 relative (quad drilling springs ≥ ~1e-9), mechanisms at ~1e-17 — ten orders of separation on both sides. - Routed all four static solve sites (`_first_order`, `analyze_linear`, `_PDelta`, `_pushover_step`) through the helper; removed the now-dead solver imports it caused. No changes to the workbench, fixture, or public API/options (`check_stability` still provides its nodal diagnostics on top).
